governingPrinciples: Semantic ownership, not current file location, determines module ownership.
Stage, Step and SPU are distinct architectural Entities with independently identifiable responsibilities and contract boundaries.
Components realize functions associated with Entities; they do not displace Entity ownership.
Composition is an aggregate responsibility owned by the Entity/Aggregate whose internal elements it coordinates; it is not a peer top-level entity or universal composition framework.
Stage Composition coordinates Step public contracts only; Step Composition coordinates SPUs and selected Supporting Units.
Functional Binding and Hierarchical Nesting are primary integration obligations. Association is only one possible relationship mechanism and is selected by contract semantics.
Core owns domain identities, contracts, semantics, results and constraints; Prefect owns native execution mechanisms, scheduling, dispatch and operational records.
Consumer owns concrete business specializations, business inputs/outputs, consumer-specific models and deployment policy.
Optional Supporting Unit patterns must not become mandatory Core dependencies for consumers that do not select them.
Advisory/conformance rules may be binding for a selected specialization without implying a runtime manager/service.
A documented contract is not evidence of an implemented runtime module or production Prefect binding.
No universal workflow adapter, scheduler, plugin manager, loader, registry, SupportingUnit base, AssociationManager or LifecycleManager is introduced without separately demonstrated need.

dependencyAndCallRules.integrationDependencyDirection: integrations.prefect depends inward on supported Core Public API; Core never depends outward on Prefect. Consumer may depend on Core and may opt into Prefect Integration.
dependencyAndCallRules.compositionDependencyDirection: The owning Composition module depends on the callable/contract surfaces of the child entities it coordinates. Child Entity and Supporting Unit modules do not import or depend on the parent Composition implementation; any target-scope relationship is expressed by specialized contract semantics, not a runtime back-reference.
dependencyAndCallRules.consumerDependencyDirection: Consumer concrete specializations implement/use GPWCF contracts; GPWCF does not import consumer models or business rules.

qualificationEvidence: PHASE-01 qualified native hierarchy and correlation; Step sibling Subflow concurrency was serialized in all 8 tested pairs, and Stage sibling Flow overlap was not deterministic (3/4).

PHASE-02 qualified same-host two-Process-Worker deployment profile: 5/5 Root runs, 10/10 Stage deployment runs, 20/20 Step subflows, 40 SPU task runs, 5/5 sibling Stage overlap and 10/10 Stage domain-result retrievals.
PHASE-02 Root-to-Stage linkage uses a synthetic deployment invocation Task Run; Stage Flow Run parent_task_run_id points to it and task_inputs.__parents__ correlates the Root dispatch Task Run.
prefectIntegrationBoundary.dependencyRule: Prefect runtime and its verified minimal integration dependency closure belong to the optional Prefect Integration installation/deployment profile, not Core. The 106-package environment snapshot is not a minimal dependency declaration.
qualificationLimits: No more than two concurrent sibling Stage qualification.

rootAndScopeRules: Pipeline Root remains an orchestration scope owned by the consumer/external workflow definition unless a separate generic Root contract is established; no Root Entity is created by inference.
Stage is the public GPWCF integration invocation boundary for a complete Stage execution; Step and SPU do not become independent Stage-level APIs.
External Workflow Framework performs actual hierarchical graph execution, scheduling and dispatch; GPWCF defines semantic contracts, constraints and result meanings.
Functional Binding is required for each GPWCF-defined executable responsibility. Relationship mechanism is selected independently by its semantics.
Association is not a universal prerequisite for binding, nesting or invocation.

errorModelIsolation.rule: Do not import the current Generator error vocabulary into baseline Core. Any generalization requires a separately versioned generic error contract, explicit ownership, full dependency closure review and approved contract changes. Until then, affected error clauses are conditional extensions and must not contaminate generic callable/result boundaries.

resultBoundaryRules: SPUExecutionResult is produced by one SPU invocation and consumed by its owning Step Composition.
StepExecutionResult is assembled by Step and returned to Stage; it is not an SPU result.
ErrorHandlerResult is an optional Error Handling pattern result and is not interchangeable with Step ErrorResult.
Stage Flow Result is Stage-owned and Stage-specific; no universal FlowResult schema is inferred.
Prefect State is operational execution evidence and never substitutes for any GPWCF domain result.
